scenes.heading: Speed, distance and time
scenes.say: How long will the road trip take? How fast was that sprinter going? Speed, distance and time are linked, and if you know any two, you can find the third.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: An airport walkway moves you 2 m every second
scenes.science: Speed 2 m/s: 10 s → 20 m; 60 m → 30 s
scenes.breaks: A walkway never changes speed. Real cars speed up and slow down, so we use average speed.
scenes.say: An airport walkway carries you two metres every second. After ten seconds you've gone twenty metres. To go sixty metres takes thirty seconds. The speed stays the same while distance and time grow together.
scenes.caption: An airport walkway carries you 2 m every second. After 10 s you've gone 20 m. To go 60 m takes 30 s. The speed stays the same while distance and time grow together.

scenes.heading: The key formula
scenes.say: Speed equals distance divided by time. Rearrange it: distance equals speed times time, and time equals distance divided by speed. Picture a triangle with D on top, S and T underneath, and cover the one you want.

scenes.heading: The D-S-T triangle
scenes.say: First the triangle, then the letters: D on top, S and T underneath. Cover the one you want. Cover S and you see D over T, so divide. Cover D and you see S beside T, so multiply.
scenes.caption: D on top, S and T underneath. Cover S: D ÷ T. Cover T: D ÷ S. Cover D: S × T.

scenes.heading: Watch the minutes
scenes.question: Chloe cycles at 18 km/h for 40 minutes. How far does she go?
lines: Speed is per hour, so use hours
scenes.say: Chloe cycles at eighteen kilometres per hour for forty minutes. The speed is per hour, so change forty minutes into forty sixtieths of an hour. Distance equals eighteen times forty over sixty, which is twelve kilometres.
scenes.caption: Chloe cycles at 18 km/h for 40 minutes. The speed is per hour, so change 40 minutes into 40/60 of an hour. D = 18 × 40/60 = 12 km.

scenes.heading: km/h and m/s
points: m/s is always the smaller number
scenes.say: To change kilometres per hour into metres per second, divide by three point six. To go back, multiply by three point six. So seventy-two kilometres per hour is twenty metres per second.
scenes.caption: To change km/h into m/s, divide by 3.6. To go back, multiply by 3.6. So 72 km/h is 20 m/s.

scenes.heading: A trip in two parts
scenes.say: Here's Max's trip, drawn as a line in two equal parts. Sixty kilometres at forty, then sixty kilometres at sixty. The parts are the same length, but the slow part takes longer, so work out each time first.
scenes.caption: Max's trip: 60 km at 40 km/h, then 60 km at 60 km/h. Same distance, but the slow part takes longer, so find each time first.

scenes.heading: Average speed
scenes.question: Max drives 60 km at 40 km/h, then 60 km at 60 km/h. Average speed?
scenes.say: Max drives sixty kilometres at forty, then sixty kilometres at sixty. That's one and a half hours, then one hour. Total: one hundred and twenty kilometres in two and a half hours, so forty-eight kilometres per hour, not fifty.
scenes.caption: Max drives 60 km at 40 km/h, then 60 km at 60 km/h. That's 1.5 h, then 1 h. Total: 120 km in 2.5 h, so 48 km/h, not 50.

points: S = D ÷ T, D = S × T, T = D ÷ S
Match units: km/h with km and hours
Average speed = total D ÷ total T
scenes.say: Quick recap. Speed equals distance over time, and you can rearrange it. Match your units, and divide minutes by sixty to get hours. Divide by three point six for metres per second. Average speed is total distance over total time. Now try the practice questions!
